<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="79.176.221.29" /></noinclude><section begin="par119" />thought applied to any kind of hostile approach, {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַם עַל־|translate=to fight against...}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָנָה עַל־|translate=to encamp against...}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽאֱסַף עַל־|translate=to be gathered together, to assemble against}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=11}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=2}}), &c.; even after verbs which express a mental action, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חָשַׁב רָעָה עַל־|translate=to imagine evil against}} any one, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|ee}}
'''4.''' Sometimes a preposition appears to be under the immediate government of a verb, which, by its meaning, excludes such a union. In reality the preposition is dependent on a verb (generally a verb of motion), which, for the sake of brevity, is not expressed, but in sense is contained in what is apparently the governing verb.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|ff}}
Various examples of this ''constructio praegnans'' have been already noticed above in ''x'' and ''y'' under {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}}; for {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=וּמִקַּרְנֵי רֵמִים עֲנִיתָ֫נִי|translate=and thou hast answered}} and saved ''me from the horns of the wild oxen'' (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=17}}, which Delitzsch translates by ''thou hast loved'' and delivered ''my soul from the pit'', read {{GHGheb|text=חָשַׂ֫כְתָּ}} with the LXX); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=12}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=זָנָה מִן־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=27}} ''to go a whoring from'' any one i.e. ''to be unfaithful to him''; {{GHGheb|text=רָשַׁע מִן־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=22}} = ''to depart wickedly from God''; {{GHGheb|text=חָרַשׁ מִן־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=28|verse=1}} ''to be silent from'' one (to turn away in silence); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=13}} [; so with {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=17}}, 30].

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|gg}}
Pregnant constructions with {{GHGheb|text=אַחֲרֵי}}: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=24}} equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=וַיְמַלֵּא לָלֶ֫כֶת אַֽחֲרָ֑י|translate=and he made full to walk}} i.e. walked fully ''after me''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=7}} read with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=חָֽרְדוּ מֵאַֽחֲרֶיו|translate=they trembled}}, i.e. ''went trembling away from him''; with {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּמַהּ אֶל־|translate=to turn in astonishment to}} some one (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=8}}); {{GHGheb|text=דָּרַשׁ אֶל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=10}}, &c., ''to turn inquiringly to'' some one; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱרִישׁ אֶל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=1}} ''to turn in silence to'' some one; {{GHGheb|text=חָרַד אֶל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=28}} ''to turn trembling to'' some one (cf. {{GHGheb|text=חָרַד לִקְרַאת|translate=to come trembling to meet}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=2}} [also with {{GHGheb|text=שאג}}, {{GHGheb|text=הריץ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שמח}} and other verbs, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; see Lexicon]); cf. further {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=1}}; with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=19}} ''he hath redeemed'' and hath put ''my soul in peace'', exactly like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=5}}; with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=7}} ''they have profaned'' and cast... ''even to the ground''; cf. 89:40.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|hh}}
'''5.''' In poetic parallelism the governing power of a preposition is sometimes extended to the corresponding substantive of the second member;<ref>Similarly the force of a negative is sometimes extended to the parallel member; see {{GHGpar|152|z}}.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=14|hidebook=1}} ''he shall perform his pleasure'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּבָבֶל|translate=on Babylon, and his arm}} shall be {{GHGheb|text=כַּשְׂדִּים}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בַּכַּשְׂדִּים}}) ''on the Chaldaeans''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=22|hidebook=1}} (but probably {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} has fallen out after another {{GHGheb|text=ל}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=10}} (perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֹשֵׁל}} may, however, be taken here as a second accusative according to {{GHGpar|117|ii}}); {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=9}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=וּמִמֹּֽקְשׁוֹת}} is to be read); {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=15|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫חַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=61|verse=7}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|ii}}
'''6.''' Adverbs which have acquired a substantival value are sometimes governed by prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־חִנָּם|translate=in vain}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַחֲרֵי־כֵן|translate=after this}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּכֵן}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=16}}) ''then, on this condition''; {{GHGheb|text=לָכֵן}} and {{GHGheb|text=עַל־כֵּן|translate=therefore}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַד־כֵּן|translate=hitherto}}.<section end="par119" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
